# Famous sculptures — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/famous-sculptures.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/famous-sculptures.ttl`](../decks/famous-sculptures.ttl) · **Cards:** 51 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

51 of the world's most famous sculptures, ranked by their number of Wikipedia and other Wikimedia sitelinks in Wikidata, from the Statue of Liberty and Michelangelo's David to Rodin's The Thinker and Louise Bourgeois's Maman (works of unknown, shared or disputed authorship left out). Front: the sculpture's title in English or Swedish, with the place or material, in brackets or in a note, where the title alone could mean another work; back: the sculptor, in the English or Swedish form of the name, with a note on collaborators or lost originals where it helps. Taken from Wikidata and checked against the English and Swedish Wikipedia, the holding museum or responsible authority where its website could be read and, for ancient works, Pliny and Pausanias.

## Licensing

The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection (the sitelink ranking), the link from each work to its sculptor (P170) and most English and Swedish titles and names come from it, so the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The English and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0), the Perseus Digital Library (CC BY-SA 3.0 US), the NPS and CIA pages (US federal works, public domain) and the pages of the Musée Rodin, the Galleria Borghese, the Louvre, HAM and Lucerne Tourism (all rights reserved) were used for verification only. Some short names that are not Wikidata labels were confirmed in the Swedish Wikipedia (Den lilla sjöjungfrun, Kyssen, Pluto och Proserpina, Lejonet i Belfort, Lejonmonumentet, Minin och Pozjarskijs monument, Chares från Lindos, the US Marine Corps War Memorial): the name of a work or a person is a fact, not a creative expression, and no wording, list or selection was taken from Wikipedia. Two Swedish name forms, Jevgenij Vutjetitj and Elgudzja Amasjukeli, are the compiler's own transcriptions of the Russian and Georgian names in Wikidata, made by the transcription rules tabulated in the Swedish Wikipedia; no Swedish text found uses them. The Swedish title of Canova's Psyche is the compiler's translation of Wikidata's French label, with the names in the form of Wikidata's Swedish labels of the depicted figures. The notes are the compiler's own wording of facts. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' licences (Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0 by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to the quoted revision; the Perseus texts under CC BY-SA 3.0 US, recorded under the CC-BY-SA-3.0 identifier because the builder has no identifier for the US port; the museums' text all rights reserved) and are short quotations given only to make the verification checkable.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators. Review by independent AI reviewers is part of the library's process; any such review is recorded as a further quality-control round, and round 0 below is the authoring agent's own checks. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Ranking (queries 1–4): as in the library's famous-paintings deck, fame is measured by the number of Wikipedia (and other Wikimedia) sitelinks of a Wikidata item. The ranking query for sculptures (instances of Q860861 or any subclass) timed out on query.wikidata.org (query 1), so it was run on QLever's mirror of Wikidata (https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata), which the famous-paintings generator also uses. A FILTER on the sitelink count returned nothing there (query 2; query 3 showed the endpoint itself worked), so the ranking takes the top N by ORDER BY … LIMIT instead. The first ranking (query 4a, top 400) lacked The Thinker: entity searches (query 5) and the class items (query 6) showed that Wikidata models works with many casts as instances of "group of casts" (Q28890616) or "sculpture series" (Q19479037), which are not subclasses of sculpture. The final ranking (query 4) therefore takes instances of sculpture or its subclasses, of group of casts and of sculpture series, top 500 by sitelinks, with each item's creators (P170). QLever's statistics (https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata?cmd=stats, read 2026-10-04) describe the index as "Complete Wikidata, TTL from https://dumps.wikimedia.org/wikidatawiki/entities (latest-all.ttl.bz2 from 10.08.2026 munged, latest-lexemes.ttl.bz2 from 07.08.2026), updated LIVE"; an independent reviewer re-ran query 4 on 2026-10-04 and got the same 561 rows and the same sitelink counts for all 51 cards. The raw CSV files were saved in the research scratch directory, which is not published.
3. Selection (see the selection): walking down the ranking of query 4, an item became a card when it is a sculptural work of art whose maker is a single, named sculptor under the standard attribution, and its title identifies it. The walk stopped at 21 sitelinks, which gave 51 cards (from the Statue of Liberty, 158 sitelinks, to Maman, 21). Each item's Wikidata entity, its creators' entities and its English and Swedish Wikipedia introductions were fetched (query 8); for every candidate with a named creator the English article was read to confirm or reject the attribution, and the articles on the rejected candidates were fetched as well (query 9).
4. Back (the sculptor): the Wikidata creator (P170) of each work. Where Wikidata lists more than one creator, the card gives the sculptor the standard attribution names and a back note names the others' roles: the Statue of Liberty (Bartholdi; Gustave Eiffel's framework and Richard Morris Hunt's pedestal), The Motherland Calls (Vuchetich; the engineer Nikolai Nikitin), The Thinker (Rodin; Wikidata also lists his founder Fonderie Hébrard, not mentioned), the Marine Corps War Memorial (Felix de Weldon; Wikidata also lists the architect Horace W. Peaslee) and the Lion Monument (Thorvaldsen's design; carved by Lukas Ahorn). For Worker and Kolkhoz Woman, Wikidata lists only Vera Mukhina; the note adds Boris Iofan's concept, from the English Wikipedia.
5. Front (the title): the English title is the Wikidata English label (or, for the Lion Monument and Hermannsdenkmal, the label the English Wikipedia uses), the Swedish title the Wikidata Swedish label where it is the Swedish name. Where Wikidata has no Swedish label or a non-Swedish one, the Swedish title was taken from the Swedish Wikipedia (query 10 and the searches of query 11): Den lilla sjöjungfrun (Den lille havfrue's article gives the Swedish name), Pluto och Proserpina (Bernini's article and the Galleria Borghese article), Kyssen (Rodin's article), Lejonet i Belfort (Bartholdi's article), Lejonmonumentet (its own article; Wikidata's sv label is the German Löwendenkmal), Minin och Pozjarskijs monument (the article on the medal For the Defence of Moscow), US Marine Corps War Memorial (its article's title; Wikidata's sv label is "US Marine Corps Memorial"). For two works with no Swedish name anywhere the Swedish front keeps the English name, as Swedish texts do (Charging Bull, The Dinner Party), and for Canova's Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss, which has no Swedish article, the Swedish front is the compiler's translation of the French title, Wikidata's fr label of Q517408 (Psyché ranimée par le baiser de l'Amour, checked by the builder), which the Louvre's page confirms: "Psyche återupplivad av Amors kyss", with the names in the form of Wikidata's Swedish labels of the depicted figures (P180 of Q517408): Psyche (Q843382), as the Swedish Wikipedia's article on her is titled, and Amor (Q5011, Cupid); both labels are checked by the builder. The form "Psyke", used in older Swedish titles such as Sergel's "Amor och Psyke", was not used because neither Wikidata nor the Swedish Wikipedia gives it for the figure.
6. Swedish names of the sculptors: the Wikidata Swedish label where it is the Swedish form (Fidias, Vera Muchina, Giovanni Lorenzo Bernini, Auguste Bartholdi …). Four are not in Wikidata in Swedish form and were checked against the Swedish Wikipedia: Chares från Lindos (Wikidata sv "Chares"; the Swedish article on 280 f.Kr. writes "Chares från Lindos", his own article "Chares av Lindos"); Hieronymus Duquesnoy den äldre (Wikidata sv "Hieronymus Duquesnoy", as the Swedish Manneken Pis article; "den äldre" distinguishes him from his son, as the English "the Elder"); Jevgenij Vutjetitj and Elgudzja Amasjukeli are the compiler's rule-based transcriptions, which no Swedish text found attests. For Vuchetich, Wikidata's sv label is the English transliteration "Yevgeny Vuchetich" and no Swedish text about him was found (query 11; a full-text search of the Swedish Wikipedia for Vutjetitj on 2026-10-04 returned nothing); his Russian name Евгений Викторович Вучетич (Wikidata ru label; given name and surname transcribed) was transcribed with the table in the Swedish Wikipedia's "Transkribering av östslaviska språk" (е at the start of a word → je, й → j, ч → tj). For Amashukeli, Wikidata's sv label is the scholarly transliteration "Elgudža Amašukeli"; his Georgian name ელგუჯა ამაშუკელი (Wikidata ka label) was transcribed with the "Transkribering" column of the Swedish Wikipedia's "Georgiska alfabetet" (ჯ → dzj, შ → sj), the convention the Swedish Wikipedia uses for Georgian names; the Swedish Kartlis Deda article's "Elgudzja Amsjukeli" was treated as a typo (an a missing). Felix de Weldon's Swedish label "Felix Weihs DeWeldon" is a full-name variant; the card uses the multilingual label "Felix de Weldon", which the Swedish Wikipedia also uses ("Felix W. de Weldon"). The English back for Manneken Pis is "Jérôme Duquesnoy the Elder", the English Wikipedia's form (Wikidata's English label is the Dutch form "Hiëronymus Duquesnoy the Elder"); the note gives the other form.
7. Disambiguation: three works share the title David (Michelangelo's, Donatello's and Bernini's), and the builder requires every front to be unique, so their fronts add the holding museum (and, for Donatello's, the material), which tells them apart without naming the sculptor. The Bargello also holds Donatello's marble David and Verrocchio's bronze David (Wikidata Q3703074 and Q2415504), so Donatello's bronze card also has the front note "nude, in hat and boots" (Wikidata P180 hat and boot; Verrocchio's David wears a leather tunic, as the English Wikipedia says, and Wikidata gives it no hat). The Pietà front adds St Peter's Basilica (Michelangelo's later Rondanini Pietà has its own card). A front note gives the place (and, where it helps, the material or subject) where a title alone could mean another work: The Rape of Proserpina (Girardon's group at Versailles and others share the title), Moses, Bacchus (with its date, since Jacopo Sansovino's Bacchus is in the same museum), Triton Fountain, The Kiss (Rodin's Paolo and Francesca, not Brâncuși's or Klimt's), The Sphere, Kryptos, Charging Bull, The Dinner Party, The Little Mermaid, Apollo and Daphne, Psyche, Maman, Cloud Gate, Kartlis Deda, Pobednik, the Lion Monument, the Monument to Minin and Pozharsky, The Motherland Calls, Hermannsdenkmal, Fallen Astronaut and the Marine Corps War Memorial. No note names or hints at the sculptor.
8. Cross-checks: every card's attribution was checked against the English Wikipedia (the sentence naming the sculptor is quoted from the full text of the revision read) and, where a Swedish article exists, the Swedish Wikipedia. Where the holding museum's or the responsible authority's site could be read, it was a further check (query 12): the National Park Service (Statue of Liberty, Marine Corps War Memorial), the CIA (Kryptos), the Musée Rodin (The Thinker, The Kiss, The Gates of Hell), the Galleria Borghese (Apollo and Daphne, David, The Rape of Proserpina), the Louvre (Dying Slave, Psyche), HAM Helsinki Art Museum (Havis Amanda, Sibelius Monument) and Lucerne Tourism (Lion Monument). Other sites refused the research environment (the National Gallery of Art, the Accademia, Britannica: HTTP 403, a certificate error) or had no usable page; those cards rest on Wikidata and the two Wikipedias. For the six lost or copied Greek works the ancient written sources of the attribution were read on Perseus (query 13): Pliny the Elder (Natural History 34.18, 34.19, 36.4) and Pausanias (1.28.2).
9. Notes: the notes are the compiler's own wording of facts; each fact has a quoted source in the card's evidence. Facts given by Wikidata (CC0) or by public-domain US government pages: the collaborators named above (Wikidata P170), the subject of The Kiss (Wikidata P180, P144), the photograph behind the Marine Corps War Memorial (Wikidata P144 and the National Park Service), the places and materials of the front notes (Wikidata P276, P186, P180), except two front-note facts that Wikidata does not give and that were confirmed only in the English and Swedish Wikipedia: Kartlis Deda's site on Sololaki hill (Swedish "Sololakihöjden", the Swedish article's form; Wikidata gives only Tbilisi) and Fallen Astronaut being left on the Moon by the crew of Apollo 15 (Wikidata gives only the location Mons Hadley). Facts confirmed in the English and Swedish Wikipedia, which only state facts that are not anyone's expression: the lost originals and Roman copies of the Greek works (and, for the lost works, Pliny), the earthquake of the 220s BC that felled the Colossus (most often dated 226 BC; the English Wikipedia's article on the earthquake says sources give 226 or 227 BC, so the note gives the decade), the 1965 replica of Manneken Pis.
10. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the work's P170 includes the sculptor, the English and Swedish labels or aliases of the work that the front uses (where the front is a Wikidata label), and the English and Swedish labels or aliases of the sculptor (where the back is one). The builder accepts a multilingual (mul) label for any language. Where the card's text is not a Wikidata label, no check is made and the evidence and round 0 say why. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).
11. The dossier was assembled by a script (make_dossier.py, in the research scratch directory, which like the other helper scripts and the saved CSV files and pages is not published) from a hand-written card list: it cuts every Wikipedia quotation verbatim from the saved article text (stopping if a phrase is not found), records the revision ids, writes the Wikidata evidence from the saved entities and generates the Wikidata checks only where the card's text equals a Wikidata label or alias.
12. Review (round 1 onwards): independent AI reviewers checked the deck for factual accuracy, language and licensing/documentation; every finding was re-verified against the sources (queries 15 and 16) before it was applied or rejected, and the outcome is recorded in the quality-control rounds.

## Selection

About 50 of the world's most famous sculptures, chosen objectively: the Wikidata items that are sculptures (instances of Q860861 or a subclass), groups of casts or sculpture series, ranked by their number of sitelinks (query 4, 2026-10-04), taken in rank order down to 21 sitelinks: 51 cards. An item in the ranking was left out when it is not a sculptural work of art (coins and currencies such as the dinars, guilders and the florin; gates, towers, columns and buildings such as the Brandenburg Gate, Trajan's Column, Nelson's Column and the Siegessäule; inscriptions, steles and tablets such as the Rosetta Stone, the Mesha Stele and the Behistun inscription; parks, museums and miniature parks; classes such as caryatid and totem pole; the toy He-Man); when its maker is unknown or anonymous (the Great Sphinx, the Venus of Willendorf, the Winged Victory of Samothrace, the Venus de Milo, the Riace bronzes, the Capitoline Wolf, the Dying Gaul, the Buddhas of Bamiyan, the Leshan Giant Buddha, the Aztec sun stone and other ancient works without a named sculptor); when it is the work of several people or a studio without one standard sculptor (Christ the Redeemer: Paul Landowski, the engineer Heitor da Silva Costa and Gheorghe Leonida, who sculpted the face; the Trevi Fountain, an architectural fountain designed by the architect Nicola Salvi and completed by Giuseppe Pannini; Laocoön and His Sons, which Pliny attributed to three Rhodian sculptors, Agesander, Athenodoros and Polydorus; the Elgin Marbles, a whole set of temple sculptures; the Holy Trinity Column in Olomouc and Mother Albania, each with three creators in Wikidata; the African Renaissance Monument, by the studio Mansudae Overseas Projects); when it was designed by one person and made or finished by others without a standard single attribution (the Merlion, designed as a logo by Alec Fraser-Brunner and sculpted by Lim Nang Seng; Mother Ukraine, begun by Vuchetich and reworked and completed under Vasyl Borodai after his death in 1974; the Crazy Horse Memorial, a mountain carving begun to Korczak Ziolkowski's design and in progress since 1948); when the attribution is disputed or rests on a hypothesis (the Bust of Nefertiti, which the English Wikipedia says is believed to be by Thutmose because it was found in his workshop; Hermes and the Infant Dionysus, whose attribution to Praxiteles the English Wikipedia calls "the object of fierce controversy"; the Apollo Belvedere, a Roman copy for which Wikidata lists an unknown maker beside Leochares; the Venus de' Medici, which Wikidata gives to Cleomenes but the English Wikipedia describes only as a copy after a sculptor "in the immediate Praxitelean tradition"; Duchamp's Fountain, a readymade the English Wikipedia calls "attributed to Marcel Duchamp"; the legendary bull of Phalaris); when Wikidata's creator is not the sculptor (Jeanneke Pis: Denis-Adrien Debouvrie conceived and commissioned it and "commissioned a sculptor to realise the design"; the Black Obelisk and the Mesha Stele, whose 'creators' are kings); when the title alone cannot identify the work or names the sculptor (the Soviet War Memorial, one of three in Berlin; the Chair of Saint Peter, both a relic and Bernini's monument around it; the Liberty Statue in Budapest, whose English name is nearly that of the Statue of Liberty); and when the sitelink count reflects interest other than the work's fame: the Wikipedia Monument in Słubice (articles written by Wikipedians about a monument to Wikipedia), and Norra skenet and Grön eld in Umeå, whose articles in the same two dozen languages (Afrikaans, Bengali, Hindi, Punjabi, Urdu …) point to a coordinated translation effort. Mount Rushmore is not in the ranking: Wikidata models it as a mountain, not a sculpture. Lost works whose sculptor is recorded by ancient writers (the Colossus of Rhodes, the Statue of Zeus at Olympia, the Athena Parthenos and Athena Promachos) and Greek works known from Roman copies (Discobolus, Doryphoros, Aphrodite of Knidos) are kept, with a note. Facts are as of 2026-10-04; a sculptor's authorship does not change, so the deck has no cut-off issue.

## Queries

**1. Ranking query on query.wikidata.org (answered "upstream request timeout", no rows): curl -s -m 170 -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql -o q1.csv** (Wikidata: sculptures (Q860861 and its subclasses), groups of casts (Q28890616) and sculpture series (Q19479037), their sitelinks, creators (P170) and English and Swedish labels)

```
SELECT ?s ?links ?sEn ?sSv (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?creatorId; separator="|") AS ?creators) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?creatorEn; separator="|") AS ?creatorNames) WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?s WHERE { ?s wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q860861 } }
  ?s wikibase:sitelinks ?links .
  FILTER(?links >= 25)
  OPTIONAL { ?s rdfs:label ?sEn FILTER(LANG(?sEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?s rdfs:label ?sSv FILTER(LANG(?sSv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?s wdt:P170 ?creator . BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?creator), "entity/") AS ?creatorId)
             OPTIONAL { ?creator rdfs:label ?creatorEn FILTER(LANG(?creatorEn) = "en") } }
}
GROUP BY ?s ?links ?sEn ?sSv
ORDER BY DESC(?links)
```

**2. The same ranking on QLever's Wikidata mirror, with a FILTER on the sitelink count (returned only the header row): curl -s -m 170 -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q2.rq https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata -o q2.csv** (Wikidata: sculptures (Q860861 and its subclasses), groups of casts (Q28890616) and sculpture series (Q19479037), their sitelinks, creators (P170) and English and Swedish labels)

```
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX wikibase: <http://wikiba.se/ontology#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?s ?links ?sEn ?sSv ?creator ?creatorEn WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?s ?links WHERE { ?s wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q860861 . ?s wikibase:sitelinks ?links . FILTER(?links >= 20) } }
  OPTIONAL { ?s rdfs:label ?sEn FILTER(LANG(?sEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?s rdfs:label ?sSv FILTER(LANG(?sSv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?s wdt:P170 ?creator .
             OPTIONAL { ?creator rdfs:label ?creatorEn FILTER(LANG(?creatorEn) = "en") } }
}
ORDER BY DESC(?links)
```

**4. The ranking query used for the selection: instances of sculpture or its subclasses, of group of casts (Q28890616) or of sculpture series (Q19479037), top 500 by sitelinks, with creators (561 rows): curl -s -m 170 -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q4.rq https://qlever.dev/api/wikidata -o q4.csv** (Wikidata: sculptures (Q860861 and its subclasses), groups of casts (Q28890616) and sculpture series (Q19479037), their sitelinks, creators (P170) and English and Swedish labels)

```
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX wikibase: <http://wikiba.se/ontology#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?s ?links ?sEn ?sSv ?creator ?creatorEn WHERE {
  { SELECT DISTINCT ?s ?links WHERE {
      { ?s wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q860861 } UNION { ?s wdt:P31 wd:Q28890616 } UNION { ?s wdt:P31 wd:Q19479037 }
      ?s wikibase:sitelinks ?links }
    ORDER BY DESC(?links) LIMIT 500 }
  OPTIONAL { ?s rdfs:label ?sEn FILTER(LANG(?sEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?s rdfs:label ?sSv FILTER(LANG(?sSv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?s wdt:P170 ?creator .
             OPTIONAL { ?creator rdfs:label ?creatorEn FILTER(LANG(?creatorEn) = "en") } }
}
ORDER BY DESC(?links)
```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 51 findings: 48 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 2 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (249 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's sculptor against Wikidata's P170, the English Wikipedia and, where available, the Swedish Wikipedia, the holding museum or authority, and the ancient sources; the English and Swedish titles and names against Wikidata labels and the Swedish Wikipedia. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 51 cards, the selection, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata's creator agrees with the English Wikipedia (and, where read, the Swedish Wikipedia, the museum or authority and the ancient sources) for all 51 cards; no card follows a value that a better source contradicts and no Wikidata check was skipped where the card's text is a Wikidata statement or label. The discrepancies are in names: Wikidata has no Swedish label, or a non-Swedish one, for several works and sculptors (handled with the Swedish Wikipedia's forms and recorded below), lists collaborators as co-creators for five works (handled with notes), and models works with many casts outside the sculpture class (handled by widening the ranking query). The builder checks P170 for every card, and the English and Swedish labels wherever the card's text is one.

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 51 cards, the description and the selection; sculptors re-checked against live Wikidata, and the builder's 237 Wikidata checks re-run.

50 of 51 cards held up. One error: Donatello's bronze David was not the only bronze David in the Bargello (Verrocchio's is there too), so the front got a note that singles it out. One warning (The Rape of Proserpina's front had no place or material although other sculptures share the title) and one suggestion (the year the Colossus fell varies by source) were applied. All three were re-verified before fixing.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| david-donatello | The front "David (bronze, Bargello, Florence)" had two right answers: the Bargello also holds Andrea del Verrocchio's bronze David (Wikidata Q2415504). | Confirmed with a live query (query 15): Q2415504, creator Verrocchio, material bronze, location the Bargello. The suggested date ("1440s") was not used, because the English Wikipedia says the date "is unknown and widely disputed; suggested dates vary from the 1420s to the 1460s". Instead the card has the front note "nude, in hat and boots" / "naken, i hatt och stövlar": Wikidata's P180 gives hat and boot (now checked by the builder, with P186 bronze and P276 Bargello), both Wikipedias describe the nude figure in hat and boots, and the English Wikipedia describes Verrocchio's David in a leather tunic. The method's disambiguation step names both other Davids in the Bargello. | fixed |
| the-rape-of-proserpina | No front note, although other sculptures share the title (e.g. François Girardon's group at Versailles). | Confirmed: a Wikidata query (query 15) lists several other sculptures titled Rape of Proserpina/Proserpine (Girardon, Vincenzo de' Rossi, Schiaffino and others). Added the front note "marble, Galleria Borghese, Rome" / "marmor, Galleria Borghese, Rom", from Wikidata P276 (checked) and P186; the method lists the card among the front notes. | fixed |
| colossus-of-rhodes | The back note gave 226 BC as settled, but sources date the earthquake differently. | Confirmed: the English Wikipedia's "226 BC Rhodes earthquake" (revision 1366274899) says "sources variously cite 226 or 227 BC". The note now says it fell "in the 220s BC (most often dated 226 BC)" / "på 220-talet f.Kr. (oftast daterad till 226 f.Kr.)", with that sentence as evidence. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language, translation and language tags (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Language, translation and language tags reviewer · **Scope:** All 51 cards (front, back and notes in both languages), the title, description and keywords; Swedish and English titles and names compared with live Wikidata labels and the Wikipedia article titles.

No errors or warnings; seven suggestions. Five were applied: the two constructed Swedish name forms now cite the Swedish transcription tables instead of articles on other people, the Dutch name form in the Manneken Pis note, the English front note of The Kiss, and two wording fixes in the description. The untagged keywords come from the builder, outside this dossier, and are left to the library maintainers.

The Prigozjin quotation was replaced by the rows е → je, й → j, ч → tj of the Swedish Wikipedia's "Transkribering av östslaviska språk" (revision 55976517), and the Russian name from Wikidata's ru label was added; the method and the licensing call the form a rule-based transcription that no Swedish text attests. The form is unchanged. | fixed |
| kartlis-deda | "Elgudzja Amasjukeli" is also constructed; the statue's Swedish article writes "Amsjukeli", and the support for the surname was an article on another person. | Confirmed. The form is unchanged. | fixed |
